html:
The Palace of the Shirvanshahs is a royal complex in the walled old city of Baku, built in the 1400s for the Shirvanshahs, the rulers of Shirvan, who had moved their capital from Shamakhi to Baku after an earthquake.

The Shirvanshahs ruled the eastern Caucasus for most of a thousand years, often as vassals of larger powers such as the Timurids and Safavids. Their palace includes a mosque, a mausoleum, a bathhouse and a court of justice, all in pale limestone with carved Arabic inscriptions. Under Shah Ismail the Safavids ended the dynasty in the 1500s. With the old city and the Maiden Tower, it is a World Heritage Site and a symbol of Baku.
